certificate.title: Build an Interactive Month-End Close Tracker with Google Apps Script Completion

course.description: Build an interactive month-end close tracker in Google Sheets using Apps Script — generated entirely by Claude. Covers the prompt, setup, testing, and customization. Inspired by Veronica Bruce.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Build an Interactive Month-End Close Tracker with Google Apps Script.

modules.description: Understand the problem and what you're going to build.

lessons.content:
Month-end close is one of the most stressful recurring processes in accounting. Teams juggle dozens of tasks across multiple people, track progress in scattered spreadsheets or email threads, and inevitably something slips through the cracks.

The typical tracking method — a shared Excel file or a checklist taped to someone's monitor — doesn't scale. It doesn't update in real time, it doesn't notify anyone when tasks are overdue, and it definitely doesn't give leadership a live view of where things stand.

What if you could build a purpose-built close tracker in Google Sheets — with a custom menu, automated status tracking, and a summary dashboard — in under 30 minutes? That's what this guide walks you through.
lessons.title: Why Month-End Close Is Broken

lessons.content:
By the end of this guide, you'll have a Google Sheet with:

- **A "Tasks" sheet** — your close checklist with task names, owners, due dates, status, and completion timestamps
- **A "Summary" sheet** — a live dashboard showing % complete, overdue items, and status breakdown
- **A custom menu** — "Close Tracker" menu in Google Sheets with options to initialize tasks, update statuses, and refresh the summary
- **A sidebar** — an HTML panel for quick status updates without editing cells directly

All of the code will be generated by Claude in a single prompt. You'll copy it into Google Apps Script, authorize it, and you're live.
lessons.title: What You're Going to Build

modules.title: Why You Need This

modules.description: Send one prompt to Claude and get everything you need.

activities.title: The Prompt to Send to Claude

lessons.content:
Open Claude and send the following prompt. Replace the bracketed placeholders with your actual close tasks:

> *"Build me a Google Apps Script project for a month-end close tracker in Google Sheets. I need:*
>
> *1. A 'Tasks' sheet with columns: Task Name, Owner, Due Date, Status (Not Started / In Progress / Complete / Blocked), Completion Date*
> *2. A 'Summary' sheet with: total tasks, % complete, overdue count, and a status breakdown*
> *3. A custom menu called 'Close Tracker' with options to: Initialize Tasks, Update Summary, and Open Sidebar*
> *4. An HTML sidebar for quickly updating task status without editing cells*
> *5. An onOpen function that adds the custom menu automatically*
>
> *Pre-populate the Tasks sheet with these close tasks: [list your actual month-end tasks here — e.g., Reconcile bank accounts, Post depreciation entries, Review AR aging, Prepare flux analysis, etc.]*
>
> *Give me the complete Code.gs and Sidebar.html files."*

**Important:** Don't leave the bracketed placeholders as-is — replace them with your real close tasks. The more specific you are, the more useful the output will be.
lessons.title: The Prompt to Send to Claude

activities.title: What Claude Will Give You Back

lessons.content:
Claude will return two complete files:

1. **Code.gs** — the main Apps Script file containing:
   - `onOpen()` — adds the "Close Tracker" custom menu
   - `initializeTasks()` — sets up your task list with formatting
   - `updateSummary()` — refreshes the Summary dashboard
   - `openSidebar()` — launches the HTML sidebar
   - Helper functions for status updates and date handling

2. **Sidebar.html** — an HTML file for the sidebar panel with:
   - A dropdown to select a task
   - Status buttons (Not Started / In Progress / Complete / Blocked)
   - Auto-refresh of the summary after each update

Keep your Claude conversation tab open — you'll reference it in the next module. You can always find it later in your Recents.
lessons.title: What Claude Will Give You Back

lessons.content:
If Claude's output doesn't quite match your needs, iterate with follow-up prompts like:

> *"Add a 'Notes' column to the Tasks sheet"*

> *"Change the status options to: Open, In Review, Closed, Escalated"*

> *"Add conditional formatting — green for Complete, red for Blocked, yellow for In Progress"*

> *"Add an email notification function that sends a summary to [your email] when the close is 100% complete"*

Claude will update the code in place. Copy the final version once you're satisfied.
lessons.title: Iterate if Needed

modules.title: Get the Code from Claude

modules.description: Create the spreadsheet, paste the code, and authorize it.

lessons.content:
Go to [sheets.google.com](https://sheets.google.com) and create a new blank spreadsheet. Name it something like "Month-End Close Tracker — April 2026".

Before you do anything else:

1. **Delete the default "Sheet1" tab** — right-click the tab at the bottom and select "Delete." Claude's code will create the sheets it needs with specific names.
2. **If Claude's code references specific sheet names** (like "Tasks" and "Summary"), those names must match exactly. Check the Code.gs file for the sheet names it expects.

**Tip:** To rename a sheet tab, double-click it. To delete it, right-click → Delete.
lessons.title: Create Your Google Sheet

lessons.content:
In your Google Sheet, go to **Extensions → Apps Script**. This opens the Apps Script editor in a new tab.

You'll see a default file called `Code.gs` with an empty `myFunction()`. You're going to replace this with Claude's code.
lessons.title: Open the Apps Script Editor
Paste the Code.gs File
Add the Sidebar.html File

lessons.content:
Go back to your Google Sheet and reload the page. After a few seconds, you should see a new **"Close Tracker"** menu in the menu bar.

Click **Close Tracker → Initialize Tasks** (or any menu option). Google will prompt you to authorize the script:

1. Click **Continue**
2. Select your Google account
3. You'll see a warning: **"Google hasn't verified this app"** — this is normal for personal scripts
4. Click **Advanced** → **Go to [your project name] (unsafe)**
5. Click **Allow**

This is a one-time authorization. The warning looks scary but it's standard for any personal Apps Script project — Google just hasn't reviewed it because it's your own code.
lessons.title: Authorize the Script

modules.title: Set Up Your Google Sheet

modules.description: Verify everything works and fix common issues.

lessons.content:
After authorizing, reload your Google Sheet. The custom **"Close Tracker"** menu should appear in the menu bar within a few seconds (it runs the `onOpen` function Claude generated in Module 2).

If you don't see it:
- Wait 5–10 seconds — custom menus take a moment to load
- Try reloading the page
- Check the Apps Script editor for any red error indicators

Once the menu appears, click each option to confirm it runs without errors:
- **Initialize Tasks** — should create/populate the Tasks sheet
- **Update Summary** — should create/populate the Summary sheet
- **Open Sidebar** — should open the HTML sidebar panel on the right

**Note:** The custom menu takes a few seconds to load every time you open the sheet. This is normal Google Apps Script behavior.
lessons.title: Verify Your Custom Menu Works

lessons.content:
Now test with real data:

1. **Initialize Tasks** — Run it and verify your close tasks appear in the Tasks sheet with the correct columns (Task Name, Owner, Due Date, Status, Completion Date)
2. **Update a task manually** — Change a task's Status cell to "Complete" and set today's date in the Completion Date column
3. **Update Summary** — Run it and verify the Summary sheet reflects your change (total complete count should increase by 1)
4. **Open Sidebar** — Use the sidebar to update a different task's status. Verify the Tasks sheet updates and the Summary refreshes

If any function throws an error, check the Apps Script editor: **View → Executions** shows a log of recent runs with error details.
lessons.title: Test Each Menu Function

lessons.content:
Common issues and how to fix them with Claude:

**"Cannot find range" or "Sheet not found" errors:**
> Go back to Claude and say: *"I'm getting a 'Sheet not found' error. Here's my error message: [paste it]. Can you check the sheet names in the code match what's in my spreadsheet?"*

**Sidebar doesn't update the sheet:**
> *"The sidebar buttons click but nothing changes in the sheet. Here's my Sidebar.html: [paste it]. Can you check the google.script.run calls match my Code.gs function names?"*

**Summary numbers are wrong:**
> *"The Summary sheet shows 0% complete even though I have tasks marked Complete. Here's my updateSummary function: [paste it]."*

**Formatting looks off:**
> *"Add alternating row colors to the Tasks sheet and bold the header row."*

Always paste the specific error message or code snippet — Claude can debug Apps Script issues quickly when it has the exact context.
lessons.title: Troubleshoot & Iterate with Claude

modules.title: Test & Troubleshoot Your Tracker

modules.description: Make it yours and roll it out to the team.

lessons.content:
Now that the tracker works, customize it for your actual close process. Go back to Claude with prompts like:

> *"Replace the sample tasks with these actual close tasks: [paste your real checklist]"*

> *"Add a 'Priority' column with values High, Medium, Low and sort by priority then due date"*

> *"Add conditional formatting: green background for Complete, red for Blocked, yellow for In Progress, gray for Not Started"*

> *"Add a 'Department' column so I can filter by team"*

> *"Create a trigger that sends me an email summary every morning at 8am during close week"*

Each time Claude gives you updated code, paste it into the Apps Script editor (replacing the old version) and save.
lessons.title: Customize Your Close Checklist

lessons.content:
To share the tracker:

1. Click **Share** in the top-right of Google Sheets
2. Add your team members by email
3. Set permissions — **Editor** for people who update task status, **Viewer** for leadership who just need visibility

To protect the structure while letting people update statuses:
1. Go to **Data → Protect sheets and ranges**
2. Protect the Summary sheet (auto-generated, shouldn't be manually edited)
3. On the Tasks sheet, protect all columns except Status and Notes

**Note:** If you added email reminder triggers, they only work with Google Workspace or personal Gmail accounts. Not all organizations allow Apps Script to send email — check with your IT team first.

**Tip:** Test the tracker yourself for a full close cycle before rolling it out to the team.
lessons.title: Share with Your Team

activities.title: What's Next — Level Up Your Tracker

lessons.content:
Once your basic tracker is running, here are prompts to level it up:

> *"Add a 'History' sheet that logs every status change with a timestamp and who made the change"*

> *"Create a Slack notification function that posts to our #accounting channel when all tasks are Complete"*

> *"Add a 'Template' sheet that I can copy each month — with a 'Start New Month' menu option that resets all statuses to Not Started"*

> *"Build a chart on the Summary sheet showing close progress over time — how many tasks were complete by Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, etc."*

> *"Add a 'Recurring Tasks' feature where tasks that happen every month are auto-populated with adjusted due dates"*

Each of these is a single prompt to Claude. The tracker grows with your process.
lessons.title: What's Next — Level Up Your Tracker
